lessons.summary: How a skill reliably detects whether it runs in the Claude Code CLI, Claude Cowork, or elsewhere. The trap: host-loop Cowork splits a skill across a host-side agent process (CLAUDE_CODE_IS_COWORK=1, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=local-agent) and a sealed-env VM shell (mcp__workspace__bash) where no CLAUDE_CODE_* marker survives -- a bare env check yields a false negative exactly when it matters. Inline !`cmd` skill-shell execution is force-disabled in Cowork (q5n) and hook exports don't cross the host/VM bridge, so neither can probe. Recipe: script-side ordered checks (IS_COWORK -> /sessions/<id> path signature -> CLAUDECODE=1 from bmt -> other), refined by the CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT value sets (c2u/u2u/d2u, normalizer cvs); content-side, branch on the tool surface (Bash vs mcp__workspace__bash). Artifact-drift caveat: the old MGn host->VM env allowlist from asar v1.6259.1 is gone from 1.18286.0 (only the unrelated SSH-MCP jBo filter remains) -- the sealed-env fact now rests on the v2.12.2 empirical probe.

lessons.title: VM Rootfs Forensics: The Mount Inventory, Session-Slug Format, and coworkd
lessons.summary: Direct forensic inspection of a third Cowork artifact class beyond app.asar and the in-VM ELF: the raw, unencrypted golden VM guest disk image (vm_bundles/claudevm.bundle/rootfs.img), which retains leftover systemd-journald log entries from real historical sessions. Extends the single verified .claude/skills mount-unit example (L104) to a full inventory (outputs, uploads, .claude, .claude/skills, .claude/projects, and one per user-connected folder), each independently mounted/unmounted per session as sessions-<slug>-mnt-<name>.mount -- and finds NO mount unit for home or /tmp, the structural reason those paths are never host-shared (they're plain guest-local paths, not bind mounts, an architecturally different kind of storage from outputs/). Confirms real session-slug values follow a Docker-style adjective-adjective-noun format. Surfaces a previously undocumented in-guest daemon, coworkd, which provisions a dedicated Unix user (uid/gid) per session slug and spawns work as that user via oneshot-<uuid> jobs -- concretely corroborating the host-loop plugin-staging mechanism (claude-hostloop-plugins/<hash>) with a real deck-review skill invocation. Notes a plausible but unconfirmed session-to-VM multiplexing inference from the idempotent user-exists check plus an observed empty vm_bundles/warm/ directory. Methodology: raw disk/container images are a searchable third artifact class when a feature isn't in either 'obvious' binary; rg is ~15-20x faster than grep -a or naive scripting-language regex over multi-GB images.

Desktop Reasoning Config: Effort & Extended Thinking Fidelity
lessons.summary: First-party binary trace of Cowork's two reasoning knobs against app.asar 1.19367.0. Extended thinking is a strict boolean -- maxThinkingTokens resolves to exactly 31999 or 0 (zgi/NX), never an arbitrary budget, delivered as --max-thinking-tokens/--thinking disabled flags with no MAX_THINKING_TOKENS env var at spawn; a live-session toggle calls query.setMaxThinkingTokens, confirming the payload behind the already-named set_max_thinking_tokens control-protocol subtype. Effort is a per-model enum (low/medium/high/xhigh("extra")/max) resolved via qgi(override, A1e(model), E2t()) across FOUR model-config classes -- literal picker models, no-picker models that still emit --effort medium, a fable/mythos regex-default class with disallowThinkingDisabled, and unknown models with no config -- all sourced from a local settings-file object (effort/effortByModel), falling back to a hardcoded "medium" string, never CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. Corrects Ch28/L114's claim that the Desktop's LocalSessions effort IPC family is backed by CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL: that env var is real but backs a separate, non-spawn-path getDefaultEffort() implementation -- the actual spawn value never touches it. Confirms setEffort's live-session branch calls applyFlagSettings({effortLevel}), giving the previously name-only apply_flag_settings control-protocol subtype its first concrete payload shape. Prompted by the claude-cowork-headless-emulator project's 2026-07-08 reasoning-config-fidelity plan (itself not yet implemented); every load-bearing binary claim independently re-derived first-party against this installation's own binary before folding in; the plan's own live-spawn-log analysis (flat 'medium' default, never per-model recommended) is relayed, not independently re-verified here.
